paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Peter is telling a worn-out church that the way through a fiery trial is to get low and trust the One who is high. He tells the elders to shepherd with a willing heart, and he tells everybody to "clothe yourselves with humility toward one another." The reason is a line from Proverbs: "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble." (1 Peter 5:5)

So humility is not about thinking you're nothing. It's about knowing whose hands you're in. Peter says to humble yourselves "under God's mighty hand, so that in due time He may exalt you," and then he says to "Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you." (1 Peter 5:6-7) I've carried worries around like a tray of cookies I was too scared to set down, and that tray gets HEAVY. God says set it down, because He's got it.

The enemy is real, and Peter tells us to be alert and to stand firm. But you're not standing alone, because your brothers throughout the world are going through the same kinds of suffering (1 Peter 5:9). And the trial has an end, because "the God of all grace" will Himself "restore you, secure you, strengthen you, and establish you." (1 Peter 5:10) So stay humble, friend, stay alert, and stay put in His grace.
